## Dead ends & gotchas (don't re-walk these)

- **React 19 + Zustand `useSyncExternalStore` ordering** — in `Lesson.jsx`, calling `graduateItem` before `setLearn` caused sessions to get stuck at `type:produce` because the store snapshot read during render was stale. Fix: `setLearn` must run *before* `graduateItem`. Burned real diagnosis time in PR #11.
- **Kana learn-step pedagogy** — `recallMode()` was returning "produce" for kana too early (asking "type the kana shown" before the learner had it memorized). Correct rule: at check2, all items use "meaning" mode (show kana → type rōmaji). "Produce" kana only kicks in at rung 3+ in reviews. Fixed in PR #13.
- **Content/engine separation is non-negotiable.** Bundling a new field or engine tweak into a curriculum PR is how the contract rots. Schema changes go in `src/data/contract.js`; engine changes get their own PR; content PRs stay content-only.
- **Never weaken a validator, assertion, or test to force CI green.** If real content or code is wrong, fix it — loosening the check defeats its purpose.
- **`LIVE_CARD_KINDS` is the forcing function.** A card kind ships only when it's in that list AND exercised by the coverage fixture. Adding `trace` or `speak` requires both — the smoke test will fail loud if one is missing.
- **Emoji in files corrupt on Windows/PowerShell heredocs** — use `create_file` with unicode escapes (`\u{2728}` etc.) instead of `cat <<EOF` containing raw emoji.
- **Cross-platform npm scripts: don't quote globs.** Linux CI runs scripts via `/bin/sh`. `node --test "tests/unit/*.test.mjs"` passes locally on Windows (Node expands the wildcard itself) and fails in CI (the shell doesn't expand quoted globs). Use unquoted: `node --test tests/unit/*.test.mjs`.
- **OneDrive causes intermittent node flakiness** in the working directory. Builds and tests pass on Vercel and fail locally for no apparent reason. Long-term move the repo to `C:\dev`; short-term, retry locally before assuming a real failure.
- **Sandbox git proxy returns 403 on remote branch deletion** — that's why the GitHub auto-delete-head-branches setting matters. Until that's enabled, dead branches pile up on the remote.
- **Don't regenerate the logo or app icons.** Use the committed skewed-rung files and the canonical SVG; CC-redrawn icons have drifted before. Treat the icon set as canonical content, not regeneration fodder.
- **The repo is the source of truth, not memory.** Reasoning about code shapes from memory is unreliable; read the actual file before changing or diagnosing it. (This rule has bitten more than once.)
- **Fix-script anchors must include the full closing `}`** of the target object. Anchoring on a partial field or a string that also appears mid-object will embed the fix in the wrong place.
- **Curriculum correctness is not schema-correctness.** `validate:content` catches structure, not natural Japanese. Verb collocations, particle usage, register, and concept-sequencing require an authoring eye. Every new unit needs Alex's line-by-line review before merge — not just CI green.
- **ElevenLabs MP3 pipeline abandoned then REVIVED** — was abandoned for Web Speech in PR #19 after rounds #15–#18 couldn't get isolated kana to pronounce right. **Root cause found 2026-06-24:** it was never a TTS limitation — it was over-loaded request params (`language_code:"ja"` + hiragana→katakana conversion + aggressive `voice_settings` stability 0.35/style 0.25 + `eleven_multilingual_v2`). A **bare `eleven_v3` call** (just `{text, model_id}`, raw character, voice defaults) pronounces single kana correctly. Confirmed by ear across multilingual/flash/turbo (all bad) vs v3 (good). The clip pipeline is back as the primary; Web Speech is now only the fallback. **Don't add language_code / katakana / custom voice_settings to the generator — that's what broke it.**
- **The conversational agent sounded good because of CONTEXT, not config.** Haruki's agent ([`BUILD-BRIEF-agent-audio.md`]) pronounces well because Claude feeds it full sentences. This briefly led to the wrong conclusion that lesson clips needed the agent or recorded human audio — they don't; bare `eleven_v3` handles isolated kana. The agent is still the right tool for live conversation, just not the only path to good clip audio.
# Lingua — Build Checklist & Progress Tracker

**Purpose:** single source of truth for project state. If Alex steps away for a while, opening this cold should answer "what's done, what's next, where did I leave off" in under a minute. Lives at repo root (`BUILD-CHECKLIST.md`); **CC (Claude Code) commits updates** to it as part of every PR.

**Roles live in `CLAUDE.md` → "Roles — read this first."** Four CC lanes: **Feature CC** (app/engine/UX, draft PRs), **Curriculum CC** (content units, self-merges on green), **QA CC** (tests + reports, builds nothing, never merges), **Idea CC** (ideation — feeds the Feature CC backlog, builds nothing, proposes only). Alex merges everything. Three report/route sections in this doc: **Feature CC backlog** (engine/app work surfaced by other lanes), **QA findings** (bugs/defects surfaced by QA, routed to a lane), and **Idea CC — feature pitches** (ranked proposals for the Feature/Curriculum lanes to pick up).

---

## How to use this doc — READ FIRST

**If you're Alex, resuming after a break:** read **Status at a glance** below, then jump to the first `[ ]` (or `[!]`) item under the current phase. That's your next action. The checked history above it is what's already shipped. Check **Dead ends & gotchas** before retrying anything that "should work" — it may already have failed for a known reason.

**If you're CC, maintaining this doc — marking protocol (follow verbatim):**
This file is updated as part of the PR that completes work. When a task is finished (PR merged to `main`), do ALL of:

1. Change `[ ]` to `[x]`.
2. Append ` — DONE <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM local>, PR #<n>`.
   Example: `- [x] Add validateContent — DONE 2026-06-21 15:40, PR #11 (CC)`
3. If the work surfaced follow-ups, add them as new `[ ]` items under the correct phase, with a one-line note on *why*.
4. Update the **Status at a glance** block (current phase, last updated, next action).
5. **Never delete** a completed task. The checked list *is* the project memory. Tasks stay in their phase section, checked in place — don't move them to a "done pile."
6. Mark work that's actively being built (PR open, not merged) as `[~]` with ` — STARTED <date>`. Flip to `[x]` only on merge.
7. Use `[!] — BLOCKED ON: <thing>` for anything stuck on a dependency (e.g. Phase 6 is blocked on the Phase 5 backend), so it's never mistaken for a plain todo.
8. When you discover a gotcha that wasn't obvious from the docs — a React 19 / Zustand ordering trap, a CI-vs-local difference, a content-contract subtlety — append it to **Dead ends & gotchas** so the next session doesn't re-walk it. Bugs fixed *within* a feature PR (like the `useSyncExternalStore` ordering fix in PR #11) should also be noted on the parent item so the history is preserved.
9. **Log everything, even concepts (Alex's standing rule, 2026-06-25).** Anything we add, change, or even just discuss as a future idea goes in this file — if it's not actionable now, park it in **Future / come back later** so nothing is lost. Don't rely on memory or chat history; the checklist is the record.

## Status at a glance


- **✅ 2026-09-13, Feature CC — THE ACCENT STANDARD IS BUILT; THE CONTENT IS WITH CURRICULUM.** Alex set the standard on 09-12 (*"accent lessons are listen, speak and type the accent, not the definition"*) and scoped it on 09-13 to **unit 1 lessons 1–3 only**. Every engine prerequisite is merged to `main`; the five unit-1 rewrites are assigned to the **Curriculum CC lead**, one branch per language off `main`, each naming its block.
  - **`type: "glyph"`** — a letter taught by its sound, `meaning: null`. Alex chose generalising `kana` over a suppression flag, and it was the cheaper option because kana already WAS this card. **Japanese provably untouched:** 175 kana items, 0 where old and new behaviour differ, 0 gaining a card kind, 50 ja-specific tests green.
  - **Typing the accent is now required** — `foldWouldEraseAnswer()`. Alex: *"If i type e and its é thats wrong dude."* He was right, and it was not merely missing: **three shipped cards were grading wrong answers correct** — `pt-u1l1-e` (é *is* vs e *and*), `fr-u6l2-a` and `pt-u12l3-a` (à vs a), whose whole point is the contrast. Narrow by design: `cafe` still passes for `café`.
  - **Speaking is graded on SOUND, not spelling** — `foldKana` passed Latin text through unchanged, so the Japanese comparison path claimed **every fr/es/pt/de/no speak card** and scored them by edit distance against the spelling. A perfect `café` transcribed `cafe` scored `hard`. The asymmetry is deliberate: typing the bare letter is the learner's error, spelling a transcript is the machine's.
  - **The Continue gate no longer waits for audio that does not exist** — it disabled the button for a full second on **1,791 silent items**, two entire languages, for a sound that was never coming. Plus a fail-open watchdog: a stalled clip used to strand Continue permanently.
  - **"Can't listen right now?"** — Alex asked for mandatory review of unheard cards and invited a better idea. The escape already grades `again`, so the scheduler brings them back; what is new is noticing the **pattern** (3 distinct items) and offering to go silent for the session. A hard gate would have locked out a learner in a library, who still cannot hear them tomorrow.
  - **`lint.js` now counts glyph cards** — it did not, while its own zero-card error read *"has no word/glyph cards"*. The first lesson written to the standard tripped the rule meant to protect it.
  - ⚠️ **ADD, NEVER REPLACE — the finding that would have cost the most.** Every word in u1 l1–3 is taught in exactly one place, that lesson, in **all five languages** (no 18/18 · fr 21/21 · es 19/19 · pt 19/19 · de 18/18). Replacing a word card deletes the word from the course — **95 core words**, including Norwegian `å være`, *to be*. Raised by the Norwegian seat; glyph cards now go in FRONT of the word cards, which also satisfies Alex's principle directly since teach order is authored order.
  - **Every existing clip survives** (no id changes under ADD). Only the **new glyph ids** need audio — **~60–80 clips, one run, after the cards exist.** An earlier warning here said the opposite; it was written for the replace plan and is corrected in `RUNBOOK` §4.

Show it" reveal will hand French learners the answer** — ✅ FIXED 2026-08-01, PR #117, **before** the audio run rather than with it, so the paid run can't ship the defect live. The reveal is now ja-only. Japanese keeps it (seeing おはよう still leaves ohayō to type, and `looksRomaji` forces a real transliteration); for a Latin script the front IS the spelling and `looksRomaji` matches any Latin letter, so it was vacuous — the escape printed the answer above the box and still granted full credit, with the ask-line literally reading "Type the word (shown)". It now degrades to the ordinary "Show answer" escape: **you still get to see it, you're graded `again`**. The hatch stays open for someone who genuinely can't hear; what goes away is credit for reading it off the screen. Also: the reveal prints `front`, not `reading` — for French `reading` is an ASCII fold (`silvousplait`), right to *accept* and wrong to *teach* — and the "Show it" link hides once the card is graded while audio replay stays.

The 15 Latin-script languages get a **sounds & accents** section instead and **never a traceable a–z** — the learner already writes those letters, so it would be busywork *and* the same "routes but doesn't teach" defect class as the `type:reading` / `build` copy-tasks caught the same day. The same carries the twelve non-modal verbs. **`aufstehen` is separable and splits in any finite main clause** (*wir stehen auf*), so it is the one item needing a modal frame to stay whole — `Wir müssen morgen aufstehen`. u20 is the only unit that can do this to itself, because it is where the modals live. So the modal frame is the only route and it necessarily imports u20 vocabulary. **One extra constraint the lead should know:** the scope pass matches surface tokens, so only the PLURAL modal forms (`können`, `müssen`, `wollen`, `möchten`) match a taught front verbatim — a singular `kann`/`soll` reads as untaught even though its infinitive is taught. - [ ] **(Feature CC) The accent fold accepts the WRONG WORD on 22 front pairs — my fix of 2026-09-13 caught only 2 of them.** Found by two crew seats reviewing that fix (block 1/pt-B1 and block 3/Norwegian), both independently, both right. `foldWouldEraseAnswer()` gates on the front being a **single character**, and that is the wrong test.
  - **What the fold does:** `normalizeReading` strips diacritics for every non-`ja` language, so two items whose fronts differ only by an accent fold to the same string and **each card accepts the other's answer**. Measured across the corpus 2026-09-13 — **22 pairs**:

    | lang | pairs | the ones that matter |
    |---|---|---|
    | **es** | **12** | `hablo`/`habló` and `trabajo`/`trabajó` — **present vs preterite**, "I speak" vs "he spoke" · `sí`/`si` (yes / if) · `tú`/`tu` (you / your) · `qué`/`que` · `dónde`/`donde` |
    | pt | 5 | `porquê`/`porque` — **same unit, same LESSON (u29l1), and their `reading` is already the identical string `porque`**, so both the typed and reading paths accept either · `às`/`as` · `nós`/`nos` · `a manhã`/`amanhã` |
    | fr | 4 | `là`/`la` · `où`/`ou` · `sur`/`sûr` · `sale`/`salé` |
    | de | 1 | `Sie`/`sie` — ⚠️ **CASE, not a diacritic** (formal vs informal "you"). My fix case-folds deliberately (`É` must pass for `é`), so this one needs a different rule again. |

Those are the literal titled targets of pt u1 l2, *"Through the nose: ão, ã, ãe"*. The one lesson whose entire subject is that diacritic does not require it.

    1. **Ambiguity:** require the exact front when another item in the same language folds to the same string. Catches all 22. Computable from the front map `contract.js` already builds for uniqueness. Leaves `café` alone, because nothing else folds to `cafe`.
    2. **Glyph type:** require the exact front for any `glyph` item, at any length — the front IS the thing being taught. Catches `ão`, `ãe` and every multigraph the five crews are about to author (`eau`, `kj`, `skj`, `sch`). This rides along with the `kana` → `glyph` generalisation Alex greenlit 2026-09-13.

The ambiguity set has to reach the checker as data: either stamped onto the item at seed time (`seedItems()` already stamps `lang`) or emitted as a generated manifest the way `audioManifest.js` is. Stamping is the cheaper of the two and has no staleness failure mode.

- [ ] **The band template's two "Conjugation drill" slots assume Romance person-marked morphology, and will break identically for every Germanic language (logged by no A2 blocks 1+2, 2026-09-06).** `scripts/scaffold-language.mjs` puts two conjugation-drill units in the A2 template for EVERY language. `conjFormsFor()` returns person-marked forms (`pres-1s` … `pres-3p`, `imperf-*`, `fut-*`). That is right for es/fr and wrong for Norwegian, where the present is ONE form for every person. Measured on `main`:
```
conjugateLatin("no", "snakke", …, "pres-1s") -> "snakker"
                                  "pres-2s") -> "snakker"
                                  "pres-3s") -> "snakker"
                                  "pres-1p") -> "snakker"
                                  "imperf-1s") -> null      (past not implemented)
LATIN_VERB_GROUPS.no === ["irregular"]
```
  A person-marked Norwegian drill is therefore **six prompts with one answer**, and the past returns nothing — `CONTENT.md`'s named defect verbatim: *"Does it route?" is not "does it teach?" — check every card kind against a new language for a prompt that is its own answer.* `conjugate-latin.js` already says as much in its own comment: *"the present — the only tense implemented — takes no class at all, so there is nothing an author could usefully assert yet."*   **This is a TEMPLATE defect, not a Norwegian one — that framing is the point.** Swedish, Dutch, Danish and Afrikaans all have one present form for all persons and will hit this identically; German hits a different version (person-marked, but with its own classes). Fixing it as "Norwegian needs an engine" fixes it once per language; fixing the template's assumption fixes it once.   **Suggested:** either a per-language form vocabulary (Norwegian wants tense-only — `pres`/`pret`/`perf` — with no person axis), or the scaffold should not emit conjugation-drill slots for a language whose engine reports no person distinction, so a crew is not handed two units it cannot honestly fill.   **Curriculum-side, already handled:** no A2 block 2 rethemed u38/u39 to the Norwegian preterite classes (-et/-te/-de/-dde), which are a real four-way system, taught as function-word vocab whose examples carry the pattern. No `pres-1s` cards were authored.

- [ ] **`lint.js` silently exempts short untaught function words — the vocab-scope check has a systematic blind spot (logged by no A2 block 1, 2026-09-06).** `src/data/lint.js:226` treats a token as an inflection, and therefore in scope, when it shares its first 3 characters with a taught stem and differs from it by ≤3 characters. That is a reasonable heuristic for morphology and a bad one for function words, because the shortest words in a language are the ones most likely to prefix a longer noun by accident. Measured on Norwegian:
```
som   UNTAUGHT  lint EXEMPTS   (matches sommer, A1 u9: 6-3 = 3)
for   UNTAUGHT  lint EXEMPTS   (matches forhold / forstå)
der   UNTAUGHT  lint EXEMPTS
om, da, hos, mot, ved, ute, selv, hele, hver, siden, mellom  — untaught, correctly flagged
```
  **Consequence:** `som` is the relative pronoun. A2 block 1 used it twice in authored u21 examples against a fully green `lint:curriculum`, and it was found by a sibling crew grepping TAUGHT-WORDS.md by hand, not by any gate. Relative clauses were unavailable to the entire A2 band and nothing said so.   **This is the same defect class as two others this project has already paid for** — a check that reports clean because it cannot see, rather than because the content is right (the A1 drill agreement regex that turned `\b` into a backspace and passed 192 drills; the duplicate-example guard that compared raw strings and never fired across 84 defects).   **Suggested fix, cheapest first:** (a) require the shared prefix to be a real morphological relation, not a bare prefix — e.g. demand the longer form ends in a known inflectional suffix for the language rather than any ≤3 characters; (b) exempt nothing below ~4 characters from the scope check, since genuine short inflections are rare and short function words are common; (c) keep the heuristic but report suppressed tokens as a NOTE so an author can see what was waved through. Any of these is Feature CC's call.   **CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY by the no A2 block-2 seat, which is stronger than the code reading above.** It ran a positive control in the same lesson, so a silence cannot be lint skipping the unit:
```
CONTROL  "Vi reiser mellom Oslo og Bergen"  -> warns: uses "mellom" before it is taught
         "Bussen som kommer er full"        -> warns about "er", "full" — som ABSENT
         "Vi reiser der i dag"              -> NO WARNING
         "Vi reiser for Erling"             -> NO WARNING
```
  **And the property that makes this worse over time: the exemption surface GROWS AS THE CORPUS GROWS.** Two of the three vouching stems are themselves recently-authored content — `som` is excused by `sommer` (A1 u9) and `der` by `deres` (A1 u12), both landed by a later A1 block. Every new long word is a potential new exemption for a short one, so a language gets less protected the more of it exists, and no gate can show it.
  **Related noise measurement, same file, worth having when writing any "verify every warning" instruction:** on the merged Norwegian A1 corpus, `er` (74) and `har` (20) were **94 of 114** warnings in one block's range — the documented morphology false-positive class. So "verify every lint warning" is in practice "verify the ~20% that are not er/har", and saying it that way makes the instruction followable.
  Curriculum-side mitigation is already in place: no A2's three crews now screen candidate fronts against `TAUGHT-WORDS.md` directly and against each other's branches, rather than trusting a green lint for short words.

Norwegian headwords verbs as `å snakke` (no/unit1.js §2, chosen because Norwegian present tense is infinitive + `-r` for every person, so one taught form is the whole present), while the example naturally shows the present: `Jeg snakker norsk.` The front is therefore never in its own sentence and `canSentence` returns false. **Measured across the two authored blocks: 0 of 54 å-verb cards can reach `sentence:build`** (block 1: 0/29, block 2: 0/25). Block 1 overall sits at 129/168 reachable (77%); of the 39 that cannot, 29 are this. **This matters more than a routing statistic**, because `sentence:build` is the only card that makes a learner PRODUCE a word order, and Norwegian is a V2 language — so the one card that could test the language's defining grammatical feature is switched off for exactly the part of speech that carries it. **Do NOT fix this in content.** Both seats considered rewriting examples into `å`-taking frames (`Det er viktig å lære norsk`) and both declined: the present tense is what an A1 learner actually produces, several of the affected examples are the blocks' deliberate fronted-XP V2 demonstrations (`I Bergen regner det mye`), and with the card hash-gated to a 25% share, block 2 measured that converting three examples buys **under one card** that actually routes. It would trade teaching for a metric. Note also that the obvious content workaround is a trap: Norwegian DROPS `å` after modals, so `Jeg kan lære norsk` is still unreachable, and the only modal phrasing that DOES tokenise — `Jeg kan å lære norsk` — is ungrammatical. **Engine-side options, cheapest first:** (a) let `sentenceTokens` match the front's LEXEME rather than its literal string — for a Latin language, try the front with a leading infinitive marker stripped (`å `/`to `) and with the language's regular present ending applied, before giving up; (b) let a content item name the surface form its example uses; (c) accept it and document that verb cards in marker-headwording languages are teach/choice/type only. Related: `LATIN_LANGS` omits `no` (separate ticket above), so there is already an open question about what the Latin verb machinery should do for Norwegian — worth solving together.

- [ ] **`normalizeReading` does not fold `ø`, and it silently strips answer tolerance from every Norwegian card containing one (logged by no block 1, 2026-09-03 — DID NOT LAND BEFORE no BLOCK 2 — NOW 29 CARDS).** `src/store/answer.js:47` special-cases `æ→ae` and `œ→oe` by explicit replace, then runs NFD. `ø` has no decomposition and no special case, so `normalizeReading("brød")` returns `"brød"` and fails the contract's `[a-z]+`. Norwegian content works around this by hand-writing those readings ø→o (`et brød` → `etbrod`), which validates — but it kills the fold branch of `checkReading` for exactly those cards, leaving only the literal-string branch. **Measured on the 12 ø cards in no block 1:**
```
FRONT "et brød" (reading "etbrod")      FRONT "en bil" (reading "enbil")
  "et brød"  PASS                         "en bil"  PASS
  "Et brød"  FAIL  <- capital            "En bil"  PASS
  "etbrød"   FAIL  <- no space           "enbil"   PASS
  "et brod"  PASS  <- the MISSPELLING passes while the correct
                      spelling with a sentence-initial capital does not
```
So a ø card loses case- and space-tolerance that all 156 other cards get free. **Fix: add `.replace(/ø/g, "o")` beside the `æ` replace in the non-`ja` branch.** Verified safe: `ø` appears in **zero** es/fr readings, so the blast radius is Norwegian only — and there is direct precedent, since that same function had ligature/accent folding ADDED when French needed it. After the fix the hand-written readings become correct-by-coincidence rather than load-bearing, so nothing has to be re-authored. Not fixed here: engine lane, and the block brief was content-only (RUNBOOK §7).

  **UPDATED 2026-09-03, after no block 2 handed back — the ticket is bigger than first filed, on two counts.**
  **(a) It affects `type:produce`, not just `type:reading`.** Block 2's fact-checker found this and it is verified here: `checkProduce` (answer.js:134) falls through to `normalizeReading(input) === normalizeReading(item.reading)` whenever `produceAllowsRomaji(item)` is true, and that returns true for **any** non-`ja` language (answer.js:124). So the dead fold branch degrades the PRODUCTION card as well. Measured on `et brød`:
```
checkProduce("et brød") true    checkProduce("Et brød") FALSE
checkProduce("etbrod")  true    checkProduce("etbrød")  FALSE
checkProduce("et brod") true  <- the misspelling again
```
  **(b) The card count is now 29, not 12** — block 1 has 12 ø fronts and block 2 has **17**, exactly as predicted when this was filed. Block 3 (u15–20) is still authoring, so the number is not final. The original filing said this SHOULD land before block 2; it did not, and block 2 shipped its 17 with the defect rather than inventing a workaround, which was the right call — the content is correct and the fix makes every hand-folded reading correct-by-coincidence, so nothing needs re-authoring whenever it lands. **One line still fixes all 29+.**

- [ ] **`scripts/check-lang-scope.mjs` cannot be used on Norwegian — its fold disagrees with the engine's, and it has no morphology (logged by no block 1, 2026-09-03).** Two separate defects. **(1) The fold is wrong.** Line 73 is `foldAccents = s => s.normalize("NFD").replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g,"")` — NFD only. `normalizeReading()` in `src/store/answer.js` additionally maps `æ→ae` and `œ→oe`, and neither handles `ø`, which has no decomposition. So the checker "expects" readings like `avære`, `eiøy` and `etkjøkken` — strings containing non-ASCII, which **`validate:content` rejects** under contract rule 9 (`[a-z]+` after normalization). Following the checker breaks a real gate, so all 6 of its reading complaints on `no` were dismissed. Fix: import `normalizeReading` from the engine instead of re-implementing the fold, and give `ø` an explicit `→o` mapping there or accept a hand-written reading. **(2) No morphology, so it flags every inflection.** Norwegian headwords verbs in the infinitive (`å være`, `å ha`, `å gå`) and nouns in the indefinite (`ei klokke`); the present (`er`, `har`, `går`) and the definite (`klokka`) then read as untaught. That is the same documented false-positive class es/fr already live with in `lint:curriculum`, which is why lint reports it as a *warning* — but this script reports it as a `✗ problem` and exits non-zero, so it reads as a failure. All 24 of its scope hits on `no` were verified by hand and every one is an inflection of a taught headword or a declared FREE cognate. Suggest it either match `lint:curriculum`'s warning severity, or grow a per-language suffix table. Not fixed here — RUNBOOK §7: never edit the rule from an authoring seat.

Content is authored to be a no-op when this lands — all Norwegian readings are already hand-folded ø→o. **Fix is one line**: add `.replace(/ø/g, "o")` beside the æ replace. Verified safe: ø appears in zero es/fr readings, so the blast radius is Norwegian only, and the same function already had ligature folding added for French.

Block 1's six, enumerated and confirmed by the fact-checker against `content/no-a1-block1`: `no-u7l1-enbat` "En båt er på en sjø." · `no-u7l1-pa` "En kopp er på et bord." · `no-u7l2-ettorg` "Et torg er i en by." · `no-u7l3-hoyre` "Ei kirke er til høyre." · `no-u7l3-venstre` "En kino er til venstre." · `no-u7l3-naer` "En butikk er nær et torg." (Block 1's other 12 indefinite-subject sentences are generic/characterizing — *En bil er dyr*, *Ei pølse er god* — and are correct; the restriction is on existence and location only.) **Not block 3's to fix** — another block's file on another branch. The fix costs no new vocab: `det` is taught at u1l2. Routed to whoever merges Norwegian A1.

Every one is a genuinely distinct Spanish word; the collision is in the ASCII fold, not the content. **Not a curriculum defect and NOT fixable in content:** deleting a card destroys that item's mastery, and merging two words into one card teaches Spanish wrongly. - [ ] **`check-lang-scope.mjs`: a multi-word front licenses each of its words separately, which hides real teach-before-use.** Surfaced 2026-08-14 closing the `está` seam. The checker splits every front on whitespace and records each word as taught at that unit (`taught.set(w, u.order)`) — deliberate, so `la casa` licenses both `la` and `casa`. But it also means unit 8's **fixed weather chunk `está nublado` licenses the bare copula `está` from unit 8 onward**, and `está` is not actually taught until unit 12 lesson 4. Consequence: the checker reported only unit 7's 10 uses, while **25 further uses in units 8–11 were invisible to it** — the same defect, one unit later, silently licensed. Those 25 are now the only Spanish teach-before-use the tool cannot see. Fix direction: only license a component word when it is a function word or when the front is article + noun (the case the split exists for), not when the front is a lexical phrase like `está nublado`, `hace calor`, `tengo frío`, `me duele`. Spanish alone has ten such chunk fronts, so this will under-report on every language that teaches phrases. Content follow-up is separate and belongs to whoever owns u8–u11 next.

The signal is now **recorded, not derived**: `startLanguage` stamps `profile.languagesChosen`, a recorded choice is never second-guessed, and pre-flag saves are matched against the cascade's *exact* shape (`["ja","es","fr"]`, in order) then **stamped with the verdict, so any save is classified at most once**. No persist bump and no migration — the flag is additive; `hydrateFromCloud` now carries it across a pull so an older device's blob can't erase it and walk the profile back into the bug.

That cost is now **pinned by a test named ACCEPTED LOSS** rather than left to be discovered. It is the cheaper of the two errors (the alternative is silently acquiring two unchosen languages, bypassing `canAddLanguage`), but it is a trade-off, not a guarantee. Caught by the truth-agent.

It now walks every language directory, takes a filter (`npm run audit -- es`), reports per-language totals, and keeps id-uniqueness global. Two exit-code holes closed at the same time, both instances of the same reassuring-green failure: **findings now set a non-zero exit** (it previously printed duplicates and issues and still exited 0, so it could never actually fail the gate), and **a bad filter argument is a hard error** (`npm run audit -- spanish` used to be dropped by the 2-letter regex and silently audit *everything* while printing a confident language list). ## Idea CC — feature pitches (logged by Idea CC — the ideation lane: proposes, builds nothing)

**Who/what:** Idea CC scans the learning-science + ND-UX space and the current app, and files **ranked, concrete, ready-to-build proposals** here for the Feature (or Curriculum) lane to pick up. Every pitch is mission-aligned (deep understanding over memorization, mechanics over dopamine, ND-first) and grounded in real file refs. Idea CC **builds nothing** — a pitch becomes work only when a lane picks it up and Alex greenlights it; big greenlit pitches get expanded into a `BUILD-BRIEF-*.md`. See CLAUDE.md → "Roles."

*Ranking key:* **[R#]** = impact-per-effort rank within the batch (R1 = do first). Lane tag on every item. Nothing here is committed until Alex says go.

### Batch 1 — first brainstorm with Alex (2026-07-04, all directions greenlit)

Alex picked all three themes (deepen understanding / reduce ND friction / smarter review) and added a mascot-cast idea. Ranked by impact-per-effort; all are approved to develop, so the rank is *sequencing*, not a cut. R2–R6 are self-contained enough to build straight from the pitch; three warranted (or warrant) a full brief.

### Batch 2 — sentence & grammar card tier (2026-07-05 brainstorm; Alex's sentence-builder + Idea CC)

**Why now:** the word-level roster is SATURATED (see roster update above). Every card tests a word or a word-in-a-sentence (cloze); **nothing tests the *sentence* itself or a *grammar transformation*.** That's the next tier — where the grammar units (U19–21: copula, particles, ～ます/ました, い/な-adj conjugation) finally get *active production* instead of recognition. Alex's "sentence builder" is the flagship.

**🔑 Shared keystone — a JA sentence tokenizer.** R11/R12 (and optionally R10) all need to split a space-less kana/kanji example sentence into **word + particle tokens**. Feasible via **greedy longest-match over the known-vocab fronts + the closed particle set** (examples are short, space-less, and built only from globally-unique already-taught fronts — the vocab-front uniqueness validator guarantees it). When a sentence won't tokenize cleanly, the card simply isn't offered (safe degradation, exactly like `canCloze`). **Build the tokenizer once → three cards ride it.** Recommend one combined brief: **tokenizer + sentence builder (R11)**, then R10/R12 fall out cheaply.

- [ ] **[R10] (Feature CC — cheapest, highest value-per-effort) Particle cloze — `cloze:particle`.** Blank the **particle** in `example.jp` (`＿` where を/が/に/で/へ/は/と/も/の/か sits), learner picks the right one from the closed particle set. The single most-drilled grammar pain point, and a genuinely distinct skill from the shipped word-cloze. **Rides the shipped cloze card** — reuses its render + `deriveGrade({kind:"mc"})`; options are the fixed particle set (no distractor-building needed). Guard: the sentence has exactly one clearly-identifiable target particle (via the tokenizer, or a tiny content tag on the target token). Smallest of the four.
- [ ] **[R11] (Feature CC — brief-worthy, FLAGSHIP — Alex's idea) Sentence builder — `build:sentence`.** Scramble the **word + particle tokens** of `example.jp` into tiles; learner reassembles them in the correct order. Add 1–2 **distractor particle tiles** so it tests particle *choice*, not just ordering. It's the token-granularity version of the shipped `build` card (which assembles a *reading* from syllable tiles) — reuse that tile mechanic + `deriveGrade({kind:"typed"})`. Tests **word order + particle placement** = the core of production grammar. Needs the tokenizer keystone; guard `canBuildSentence`. Slots at the PRODUCED tier (rung 3). **This is the one to brief first.**
- [ ] **[R12] (Feature CC — rides R11) English → Japanese sentence production — `produce:sentence`.** Show only `example.en`, JA hidden; learner builds the JA sentence from tiles (R11's mechanic + a pool of plausible distractor words/particles). Because the reference sentence is hidden, it's **genuine production from meaning** — the deepest production short of free writing, yet ND-safe (tile assembly, not a blank page). Reuses R11's tokenizer + tile UI. Slots at top-of-PRODUCED / pre-SPOKEN — the "can you say it in Japanese?" bar, in tile form.
- [ ] **[R13] (Feature CC — ⚠️ needs new content data) Conjugation transform — `conjugate`.** Given a base/dictionary form + a target inflection (past ました · neg ません · plain ない · い-adj くない · past-adj かった · want たい), learner produces the conjugated form (tiles or typed → reuse `checkReading`). **Nothing tests grammatical *transformation* today**, and A1's whole grammar tail *is* conjugation. The one card with a real content cost: it needs **conjugation-pair data** (base → {past, neg, …}) = a schema/content addition (Curriculum + `contract.js`), unlike R10–R12 which reuse existing `example` data. Highest grammar-transformation value; ranked last only for that data dependency. *Route the data half to Curriculum CC once scoped.*

### Batch 6 — motivation model DECIDED (2026-07-10)

**Alex's philosophy call (2026-07-10):** asked "add more achievements?" + "get rid of streak/XP/freezes?", he chose **structural milestones only**. The line is **capability vs activity** — capability milestones (mark real skill gained) are the mission-aligned progress signal and get built; engagement rewards (streak/XP/freezes/day-counts) reward activity and are OUT. Codified in CLAUDE.md's anti-gamification rule the same day. This **confirms R17 / R18 / R30 as GO** (they were pending Alex's call).

Guardrail: milestones reward **capability, never activity** (no points/streaks/decay/FOMO). ⚠️ Removing streak/XP/freeze fields = persist/user-state change → Alex's check-in, migration-safe. Brief has the milestone catalog, phases (M.0 selector+tests first), and DoD.

**JOB 4 — scaffolds validate, but they COLLIDE WITH EACH OTHER.**

- **[P1] `de`, `no`, `pt` conflict pairwise on 3 files** — `src/data/index.js`, `src/data/companions.js`, `server/companions.js`. `de` merged clean only because it went first; `no` and `pt` each hit **3 conflicts**. The collisions are purely additive (each registers its own import, `UNITS` spread and companion entry on the same lines), so the resolution is **union, not a winner** — but it must be done by hand three times, and **a naive "keep both" silently swallows the `},` that closes the previous companion entry**, producing a syntax error reported ~24 lines later. I hit exactly that. Merge one at a time and run `node --check server/companions.js` after each.
- After union resolution: **527 units, 6 companions (ja es fr de no pt), validate 0 err, 313/313, audit unchanged at 11,246 items.**

- **Onboarding gate: the fix is CORRECT AND NECESSARY — verified at the data level.** `itemCount()` returns **0 playable items** for de/no/pt and the picker gates `onClick` on `l.cards > 0`. The pre-fix logic (`UNITS.some(u => u.lang === id)`) returns **true** for all three scaffolds, so without this fix all three would have been pickable and would have booted into an empty language.
- **[BLOCKED] The onboarding flow itself cannot be exercised here.** `App.jsx:32` sets `AUTH_ENABLED = supabase configured && !IS_WEBDRIVER`, putting the whole auth+onboarding block behind a flag that is FALSE under Playwright. Spoofing `navigator.webdriver` flips it true, and the app then demands a real Supabase login — the automated path lands on `<Auth />`. **The same flag also gates audio playback**, so no single automated run can have both app access and working audio.

**JOB 3 — one verdict delivered, one blocked.**

The double-reset race and the "saved to your account" vs "saved on this device" receipt are both **unverified**. This is the highest-risk unverified item in the merge.

Routing is fine (**1,177 es items DO route to listen:type**), so the bug is `cardPreviewRoute('listen:type','es')` seeding an item that does not route there. It matters because that preview is the exact tool for eyeballing this change.
  - **Accent tolerance PASSES in both languages.** Twelve accented items sampled; every one grades correct **with and without** diacritics (`très`/`tres`, `el año`/`el ano`, `s'il vous plaît`, `el lápiz`). Worth knowing it is that permissive: stripping ñ means `el ano` is accepted for `el año`.
  - **Audible quality remains unverified** — audio is suppressed under WebDriver by design, so "does the clip sound right" is still an ear check only Alex can do.

**JOB 5 — the 2,041 warnings are about 2.5% real. Not a crisis, and not a reason to hold anything.**

- **All 2,041 are Latin-only: es 1,451 / fr 588 / ja 0.** Japanese has 2 lesson-size advisories and zero teach-before-use. Whatever the checker does, ja does not trip it.

- **1 genuine defect in 40 = 2.5%.** `fr-u117l3-application` uses "doivent" and **`devoir` is taught nowhere in French** — verified against every fr front.
- **Extrapolated: roughly 50 real teach-before-use defects corpus-wide.** A real Curriculum backlog, but small. The lint's own advisory line is accurate: morphology and cognates dominate, at roughly nine false alarms per real one.
- **[P2] (Feature CC, cheap) The checker does not exempt the item's own headword.** Five of the 40 sampled warnings flag a conjugation of the very word the card teaches. Exempting `item.front`'s own inflections would strip a large slice of the noise for free and make the rest worth reading.

Requested by Alex during the Pre-A1/A1 pass. Kept simple; **all are Feature-CC lane** (new card kinds = `LIVE_CARD_KINDS` + coverage fixture = engine/schema, draft PR, Alex's call) unless tagged Curriculum. Ranked by impact-per-effort.

First card that trains **listening → recognition**; today every card shows the glyph. **Key design call (in the brief): it's a card *variant*, NOT a new rung** — reuses `ChoiceCard` grading + `useItemAudio`, so zero change to rungs/FSRS/mastery/schema; the only `contract.js` edit is adding the kind to `LIVE_CARD_KINDS`. Needs a routing guard (audio manifest) so a listen card never serves a silent item, + the coverage fixture. Brief has ground-truth file refs, open decisions, and build phases. Pairs with the dormant `speak` card (hear ↔ say) but ships far cheaper (no capture/vendor/backend).
- [~] **(Feature CC) Reverse recognition — EN → JA choice (`choice:reverse`). STARTED 2026-07-11 (feat/reverse-recognition).** Current `choice` shows the JA glyph and asks the meaning (JA→EN). Add the mirror: show the English, pick the correct kana/kanji from 4 options. Strengthens recall in the *production* direction with far less friction than typing. **Shipped:** `ChoiceCard` gains a `reverse` prop (English prompt + glyph `front` options via `buildOptions(...,"front")` + `data-card-kind`); `shouldReverseChoice` in `cardRouting.js` (vocab-with-meaning, salted independent hash band `REVERSE_SHARE=0.4`); routed in `Review.reviewStepFor` at the **recognition rung (≤1)**, checked after `shouldListen` — rung 1 now interleaves listen:choice / choice:reverse / choice; added to `LIVE_CARD_KINDS` (+ pinned test), Dev Quick-card ("Reverse"), and the smoke coverage fixture (`ja-u1l3-sakana`). ⚠️ **DECISION FOR ALEX (one-line to change):** placed at the **recognition rung interleaved with choice**, **40% share** of eligible non-listen vocab — the obvious default, but the rung/share are yours to tune (`REVERSE_SHARE` + the `reviewStepFor` order).

Enhancement (not a new kind): when the item is kana, prefer visually-confusable peers as the wrong options. Needs a small confusable-set map (~8 pairs); makes the recognition card actually test what the hints teach.

**Verdict: A1 is in good shape — no hard bugs.** No crashes, no duplicate item ids, no duplicate vocab fronts, no validator/lint failures. Findings below are **naturalness/pedagogy items for the batched native review** (the gate that already governs kanji+grammar) — none block.

- [ ] **P2 — Forward kanji references in kanji-unit examples (confirmed + enumerated; was flagged generically).** A kanji appears in an example before its own teaching unit: **U13** 電→`電車で行きます` (車 is U18, 行 is U17); **U13** 気→`元気ですか` (元 is U18); **U14** 友→`友だちが来ます` (来 is U17); **U14** 先→`先生に聞きます` (聞 is U17); **U14** 手→`手を見ます` (見 is U17); **U14** 足→`足が長いです` (長 is U18). Learner meets the glyph as "unknown kanji" mid-example. **Fix (Curriculum CC, native-review batch):** either write these examples in kana until the kanji is introduced, or reorder the kanji units to the category scheme (⚠️ id-churn resets that kanji's mastery — do it in the same deliberate pass, pre-users).

So for 大/小 the shown reading doesn't match the reading in the example sentence (confusing at recognition time). **Fix (Curriculum CC, native-review):** give 大/小 the kun reading (おお…/ちい…) for consistency, or split the on/kun explicitly in the hint. Additive if only the `reading`/`hint` change; id-safe.

Keep it calm/ND-friendly, no streak-bait. Likely its own small PR with Alex feel-check.

Good candidates that drill real recall: kana↔romaji matching/pairs, speed-recognition (timed but gentle), listening "which kana did you hear", sentence/word build-from-tiles against the clock. Each should run on the existing item/SRS data (a game session can feed grades back into FSRS so playing = reviewing). Decide whether they're a separate tab or woven into the session. Its own sprint; scope when picked up.
- **Standard language pathway — see `BUILD-BRIEF-language-blueprint.md` (Alex, 2026-08-02): "we need a standard so creating other languages is easy and I can mass-do it with multiple CC running."** Correct read — there was no written standard, only French's de-facto one. **Japanese is the model** (Alex's call 2026-08-02 — "follows the structure of ja since that one is basically done right"). The brief extracts ja's actual shape: **three interleaved strands per CEFR band** — script/sound (taught in chunks that are immediately used for real words: ja U1 = 25 kana + 29 vocab), thematic vocab, and grammar-as-function-word-vocab (copula → verbs & particles → past tense & agreement) — plus a **coverage pass** closing each band. **A Latin-script language is the identical template with the script strand collapsed to one unit**; that's the only difference. Density = the mature ja shape, **4 lessons × 6 cards = 24 cards/unit** (u22 onward; ja's 47–55-card U1–U10 are pre-lint drift, explicitly not the model — fr independently landed at 21, same target). Also flagged: ja's `order`/`stage` interleave inconsistently (pre-a1 reappears at u16, a1 at u53–68 and u82–87) — a new language keeps `order` monotonic within `stage`. Operational half is `RUNBOOK-new-language.md` (§0 = the one line Alex types; §7 = the stuck-table that makes it no-questions-asked). B1/B2 spine unspecified until ja gets there. **Prerequisites: (a)(b)(c) ✓ DONE 2026-08-02, branch `feat/language-prereqs` (commit `aefa82f`) — draft, awaiting Alex's merge.** Full gate green (validate, lint, 189 unit tests, audit, build, Playwright dev 27 + preview 25). Shipped with it: **`isLive` now requires *playable* content** — a scaffolded language of locked stubs was flipping live with nothing learnable, which `tests/unit/prune-languages.test.mjs` caught because it would also have defeated the stale-save migration in `useStore`. **(d) downgraded — not a blocker** (see below). The four as originally filed: (a) **word-front uniqueness is global across languages** — `contract.js` + `lint.js` key the map on `front` with no lang, so es `no` + it `no` is a hard CI failure (verified by running `validateContent` directly); it fails at *merge* time, so parallel sessions are each green alone and red together; (b) `src/data/index.js` is a merge-conflict funnel (one import + one array entry per unit in a single shared file) → generate a per-language barrel instead (**not** `import.meta.glob` — Vite-only, and the `node --test` unit tests import that file); (c) no `scaffold:lang` script, so a new language starts by hand-copying an existing one; (d) ~~the `reading` contract blocks 5 languages outright~~ — **CORRECTED 2026-08-02 after testing both paths: nothing is blocked.** Readings are authored as the *ASCII fold* (the French convention: `s'il vous plaît` → `silvousplait`), so Norwegian authors `øl` → `ol` and validates clean; and a learner typing the real word is still accepted because `checkReading` matches `raw === item.front` before folding. The genuine defect is narrower and already live: **`reading` is *displayed* as a pronunciation guide** while being an ASCII typing key — filed as a Feature CC item above. The lossy-fold issue for tonal languages (`ma má mà mả mã mạ` → all `ma`) is real but deferred until a tonal language is scheduled. **Crews are not blocked by (d).**
- **AI tiers = the monetization model (Alex, 2026-08-02) — not scoped yet; revisit when ja hits B2.** The plan in Alex's words: AI access starts **limited** for everyone; as a learner progresses, the app **requires** conversation with the AI so they actually practise speaking. **Free** users get that progression-gated practice only. **Paid** users get open-ended AI — "ask it to translate a song, ask about words, just have conversations" — i.e. the tutor as a general tool, not only a drill partner. **Timing:** attack this once **Japanese is finished through B2**; ja sets the standard and the other languages copy it *(unless French finishes first — then fr sets it)*. Nothing to build now; this is the shape to design against. Infrastructure already in place: the Haruki tab (Phase 6.5, PR #29) is a live ElevenLabs Conversational Agent, and `inventoryFor({lang, maxLevel, maxRung})` already scopes what the tutor may see by CEFR + rung — that selector is the natural lever for "AI unlocks as you climb."
  - **Open questions to settle when we attack it** (log only, no decision yet): (1) **Cost floor** — conversational minutes bill per minute, so "limited" needs a real unit (minutes/day? turns/session?) before pricing means anything. (2) **Required-conversation vs. the anti-burnout spine** — a *required* AI turn that a learner can't complete (mic anxiety, no quiet room, ND load) becomes a hard blocker on the ladder; needs a non-speaking fallback path (text chat already exists in the unified Haruki chat) so the requirement gates *practice*, not *progress*. (3) **Free-tier honesty** — what a free user is promised up front, so the paywall reads as "more tool," never as "we took your tutor away." (4) Payments/entitlements = new dependency + backend scope (Phase 6 territory), its own brief.
- **Sign language — PARKED, and it gets its OWN STRUCTURE (Alex, 2026-09-03).** Decided after scoping it: *"we'll add it later, it'll have its own structure."* Not a catalog entry, not the language blueprint, not a `LANGUAGES[]` row — a second modality alongside the existing one. Do not try to fit it into `src/data/<lang>/` conventions when it comes.
  - **Why it cannot reuse the structure.** Two load-bearing assumptions break. (1) **There is no typeable `front`.** A sign is handshape + location + movement + palm orientation + non-manual markers; the written stand-ins are all wrong for teaching — *gloss* (`MOTHER`, `GO-TO`) is an English label for a sign, so teaching gloss teaches English, and HamNoSys/SignWriting are real notation nobody reads and no keyboard types. `front` has to be **video**, which kills every card that types or manipulates a string: `type:meaning`, `type:produce`, `build`, `cloze:choice`, `sentence:build`. (2) **Audio is the perception channel** — `listen:choice`, `listen:type` and `speak` all die with it. Add that ASL grammar is topic-comment with spatial agreement and classifiers, carried in **simultaneous non-manual markers** rather than word order, so the blueprint's "grammar as function-word vocab" has nothing to attach to.
  - **"Sign language" is not one language.** ASL · BSL · LSF · Auslan are unrelated — BSL and ASL are not mutually intelligible (ASL descends from LSF). Whatever the structure is, it is per-language like everything else.
  - **What the engine already gives for free:** media is a **manifest of item ids** (`AUDIO_IDS.has(item.id)` → `public/audio/<id>.mp3`), so a parallel `VIDEO_IDS` → `public/video/<id>.mp4` with `hasVideo()` is small, and the routing gates already branch on `hasAudio`. FSRS, the rungs, the daily loop and milestones are modality-agnostic and need nothing.
  - **The wall is production grading.** Typing and STT both die. Self-assessment is honest but gives FSRS a self-reported grade (a real weakening of the signal); in-browser hand/pose tracking handles isolated handshapes and is an open research problem for real signing with coarticulation and non-manuals — **a confidently wrong grade is worse than no grade**; human review does not scale. Settle this before authoring anything.
  - **The strategic fact, and the reason it is parked behind de/no/pt:** every other language scales through TTS — one paid `generate:audio` run and the band is voiced. **There is no TTS for sign.** Every clip is human-produced or licensed, forever, thousands per band. It is the first language whose content cost does not fall with scale. It also requires **Deaf signers producing the content** — not a nice-to-have; a hearing-built ASL course is a known failure mode and would be judged as one.
  - **The first slice, when it is picked up: FINGERSPELLING, on its own.** The manual alphabet is a closed set of 26 handshapes, structurally identical to kana — one glyph, one meaning, no grammar — so `front` stays typeable (the letter) and recognition/production work today's way. **Receptive fingerspelling** (reading a fingerspelled word at speed) is the genuinely hard and useful skill, and it is `listen:choice` with video swapped for audio. **~30–100 clips, not thousands.** It proves the video manifest, the card kinds and the Deaf-consultant relationship before anyone commits to a curriculum.
- **Dress Lingua up to match the language (Alex, 2026-06-25) — big effort, its own sprint.** The mascot (Lingua the panda) should be costumed/themed per the language being learned — e.g. Japanese touches for ja, a beret for fr, etc. Alex flags this as needing "some good time" — likely new art generation per language × the existing pose set (base/wave/proud/cheer/celebrate/sleepy/think/wistful), kept consistent. **Mascot art is Grok-generated** (Alex will supply more clips/poses); plan an attribution line ("made with Grok") where appropriate. Decide art pipeline, keep transparency-clean (re-run `strip-mascot-bg.mjs`). Ties into per-language identity + companion screens.

## Dead ends & gotchas (don't re-walk these)

- **React 19 + Zustand `useSyncExternalStore` ordering** — in `Lesson.jsx`, calling `graduateItem` before `setLearn` caused sessions to get stuck at `type:produce` because the store snapshot read during render was stale. Fix: `setLearn` must run *before* `graduateItem`. Burned real diagnosis time in PR #11.
- **Kana learn-step pedagogy** — `recallMode()` was returning "produce" for kana too early (asking "type the kana shown" before the learner had it memorized). Correct rule: at check2, all items use "meaning" mode (show kana → type rōmaji). "Produce" kana only kicks in at rung 3+ in reviews. Fixed in PR #13.
- **Content/engine separation is non-negotiable.** Bundling a new field or engine tweak into a curriculum PR is how the contract rots. Schema changes go in `src/data/contract.js`; engine changes get their own PR; content PRs stay content-only.
- **Never weaken a validator, assertion, or test to force CI green.** If real content or code is wrong, fix it — loosening the check defeats its purpose.
- **`LIVE_CARD_KINDS` is the forcing function.** A card kind ships only when it's in that list AND exercised by the coverage fixture. Adding `trace` or `speak` requires both — the smoke test will fail loud if one is missing.
- **Emoji in files corrupt on Windows/PowerShell heredocs** — use `create_file` with unicode escapes (`\u{2728}` etc.) instead of `cat <<EOF` containing raw emoji.
- **Cross-platform npm scripts: don't quote globs.** Linux CI runs scripts via `/bin/sh`. `node --test "tests/unit/*.test.mjs"` passes locally on Windows (Node expands the wildcard itself) and fails in CI (the shell doesn't expand quoted globs). Use unquoted: `node --test tests/unit/*.test.mjs`.
- **OneDrive causes intermittent node flakiness** in the working directory. Builds and tests pass on Vercel and fail locally for no apparent reason. Long-term move the repo to `C:\dev`; short-term, retry locally before assuming a real failure.
- **Sandbox git proxy returns 403 on remote branch deletion** — that's why the GitHub auto-delete-head-branches setting matters. Until that's enabled, dead branches pile up on the remote.
- **Don't regenerate the logo or app icons.** Use the committed skewed-rung files and the canonical SVG; CC-redrawn icons have drifted before. Treat the icon set as canonical content, not regeneration fodder.
- **The repo is the source of truth, not memory.** Reasoning about code shapes from memory is unreliable; read the actual file before changing or diagnosing it. (This rule has bitten more than once.)
- **Fix-script anchors must include the full closing `}`** of the target object. Anchoring on a partial field or a string that also appears mid-object will embed the fix in the wrong place.
- **Curriculum correctness is not schema-correctness.** `validate:content` catches structure, not natural Japanese. Verb collocations, particle usage, register, and concept-sequencing require an authoring eye. Every new unit needs Alex's line-by-line review before merge — not just CI green.
- **ElevenLabs MP3 pipeline abandoned then REVIVED** — was abandoned for Web Speech in PR #19 after rounds #15–#18 couldn't get isolated kana to pronounce right. **Root cause found 2026-06-24:** it was never a TTS limitation — it was over-loaded request params (`language_code:"ja"` + hiragana→katakana conversion + aggressive `voice_settings` stability 0.35/style 0.25 + `eleven_multilingual_v2`). A **bare `eleven_v3` call** (just `{text, model_id}`, raw character, voice defaults) pronounces single kana correctly. Confirmed by ear across multilingual/flash/turbo (all bad) vs v3 (good). The clip pipeline is back as the primary; Web Speech is now only the fallback. **Don't add language_code / katakana / custom voice_settings to the generator — that's what broke it.**
- **The conversational agent sounded good because of CONTEXT, not config.** Haruki's agent ([`BUILD-BRIEF-agent-audio.md`]) pronounces well because Claude feeds it full sentences. This briefly led to the wrong conclusion that lesson clips needed the agent or recorded human audio — they don't; bare `eleven_v3` handles isolated kana. The agent is still the right tool for live conversation, just not the only path to good clip audio.
# Lingua — Build Checklist & Progress Tracker

**Purpose:** single source of truth for project state. If Alex steps away for a while, opening this cold should answer "what's done, what's next, where did I leave off" in under a minute. Lives at repo root (`BUILD-CHECKLIST.md`); **CC (Claude Code) commits updates** to it as part of every PR.

**Roles live in `CLAUDE.md` → "Roles — read this first."** Four CC lanes: **Feature CC** (app/engine/UX, draft PRs), **Curriculum CC** (content units, self-merges on green), **QA CC** (tests + reports, builds nothing, never merges), **Idea CC** (ideation — feeds the Feature CC backlog, builds nothing, proposes only). Alex merges everything. Three report/route sections in this doc: **Feature CC backlog** (engine/app work surfaced by other lanes), **QA findings** (bugs/defects surfaced by QA, routed to a lane), and **Idea CC — feature pitches** (ranked proposals for the Feature/Curriculum lanes to pick up).

---

## How to use this doc — READ FIRST

**If you're Alex, resuming after a break:** read **Status at a glance** below, then jump to the first `[ ]` (or `[!]`) item under the current phase. That's your next action. The checked history above it is what's already shipped. Check **Dead ends & gotchas** before retrying anything that "should work" — it may already have failed for a known reason.

**If you're CC, maintaining this doc — marking protocol (follow verbatim):**
This file is updated as part of the PR that completes work. When a task is finished (PR merged to `main`), do ALL of:

1. Change `[ ]` to `[x]`.
2. Append ` — DONE <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM local>, PR #<n>`.
   Example: `- [x] Add validateContent — DONE 2026-06-21 15:40, PR #11 (CC)`
3. If the work surfaced follow-ups, add them as new `[ ]` items under the correct phase, with a one-line note on *why*.
4. Update the **Status at a glance** block (current phase, last updated, next action).
5. **Never delete** a completed task. The checked list *is* the project memory. Tasks stay in their phase section, checked in place — don't move them to a "done pile."
6. Mark work that's actively being built (PR open, not merged) as `[~]` with ` — STARTED <date>`. Flip to `[x]` only on merge.
7. Use `[!] — BLOCKED ON: <thing>` for anything stuck on a dependency (e.g. Phase 6 is blocked on the Phase 5 backend), so it's never mistaken for a plain todo.
8. When you discover a gotcha that wasn't obvious from the docs — a React 19 / Zustand ordering trap, a CI-vs-local difference, a content-contract subtlety — append it to **Dead ends & gotchas** so the next session doesn't re-walk it. Bugs fixed *within* a feature PR (like the `useSyncExternalStore` ordering fix in PR #11) should also be noted on the parent item so the history is preserved.
9. **Log everything, even concepts (Alex's standing rule, 2026-06-25).** Anything we add, change, or even just discuss as a future idea goes in this file — if it's not actionable now, park it in **Future / come back later** so nothing is lost. Don't rely on memory or chat history; the checklist is the record.

## Feature CC backlog (logged by curriculum CC — app/engine lane, not mine to build)

Single place for the feature/engine work that's surfaced. Curriculum CC adds here; **feature CC builds.** Detail/rationale for each is in the status block above and the linked briefs.

- [ ] **`check-lang-scope.mjs`: a multi-word front licenses each of its words separately, which hides real teach-before-use.** Surfaced 2026-08-14 closing the `está` seam. The checker splits every front on whitespace and records each word as taught at that unit (`taught.set(w, u.order)`) — deliberate, so `la casa` licenses both `la` and `casa`. But it also means unit 8's **fixed weather chunk `está nublado` licenses the bare copula `está` from unit 8 onward**, and `está` is not actually taught until unit 12 lesson 4. Consequence: the checker reported only unit 7's 10 uses, while **25 further uses in units 8–11 were invisible to it** — the same defect, one unit later, silently licensed. Those 25 are now the only Spanish teach-before-use the tool cannot see. Fix direction: only license a component word when it is a function word or when the front is article + noun (the case the split exists for), not when the front is a lexical phrase like `está nublado`, `hace calor`, `tengo frío`, `me duele`. Spanish alone has ten such chunk fronts, so this will under-report on every language that teaches phrases. Content follow-up is separate and belongs to whoever owns u8–u11 next.

- [x] **(Feature CC) The three blockers the Spanish crew hit — ✓ DONE 2026-08-05, branch `fix/language-crew-blockers` (draft — Alex merges).** All surfaced by the es block-1 hand-back, all outside the Curriculum lane, fixed together because they share one cause: *engine behaviour derived from which languages happen to have content.*
  1. **`pruneStartedLanguages` could not survive its own success.** It inferred "this save carries the retired ja→es→fr cascade seeding" from *a listed language having no content* — sound reasoning (`startLanguage` is content-gated) with a fuse on it, because it only holds while some cascade language is unauthored. French shipping burned half of it; Spanish shipping burned the rest. With ja/es/fr all live the test is false for the very profile it exists to catch, so **nothing was pruned and a pre-language-choice save silently gained two started languages, bypassing `canAddLanguage`** — the same defect fixed on 2026-07-31, back by decay rather than by edit. The signal is now **recorded, not derived**: `startLanguage` stamps `profile.languagesChosen`, a recorded choice is never second-guessed, and pre-flag saves are matched against the cascade's *exact* shape (`["ja","es","fr"]`, in order) then **stamped with the verdict, so any save is classified at most once**. No persist bump and no migration — the flag is additive; `hydrateFromCloud` now carries it across a pull so an older device's blob can't erase it and walk the profile back into the bug.
  ⚠️ **The fingerprint is NOT collision-free, and an earlier draft of this entry wrongly called the design "non-destructive by construction."** A pre-flag save from a learner who genuinely started those three languages in that order is *indistinguishable* from the seeding, because the distinguishing fact was never recorded — so in that one case a deliberately-started, untouched, non-active language is dropped and must be re-added. That cost is now **pinned by a test named ACCEPTED LOSS** rather than left to be discovered. It is the cheaper of the two errors (the alternative is silently acquiring two unchosen languages, bypassing `canAddLanguage`), but it is a trade-off, not a guarantee. Caught by the truth-agent.
  Scope of the decay claim, narrowed: the **staleness test** no longer consults content and cannot decay as languages ship. The `kept` filter still does — so a *recorded* choice is now exempt from it entirely, because otherwise holding `es` back (a live possibility given the red merge below) would silently delete Spanish from every profile that started it.
  **Browser evidence, stated precisely:** on a tree with all 20 Spanish units merged, two cases were checked end-to-end — a stale `["ja","es","fr"]` save boots to `["ja"]`, and a learner who chose Spanish keeps `["es"]`. Both are cases that *should* succeed; the risky case above is undecidable by construction and was not browser-checked. The throwaway branch was deleted, so no artifact of that run survives in the repo.
  2. **Two more surfaces leaked the ASCII fold, and one of them was the loud one.** `db5e45c` gated Teach/Speak/Trace on `readingIsInformative` — from memory, not from a list — and missed both the Ladder word-bank row (`Ladder.jsx`, 12px grey) and **`GlyphDetail.jsx:78`, the modal that row opens on tap, which printed the fold at 22px bold accent with *no gate at all*, not even `showRomaji`.** Fixing only the row would have moved the leak, not closed it. Both now use the same helper. **The method that missed them twice was not running `grep -rn "\.reading}" src/`, which returns the complete five-surface list in one line** — that grep is the actual lesson, and it's how the truth-agent found GlyphDetail after the fact-checker had already found Ladder. This is live for **French A1 today** (566 items), not just for unshipped Spanish. ⚠️ **Honest limit:** both fixes are by inspection plus the helper's unit tests — I could never get the word bank to render a Spanish word in a scripted browser run (even at rung 3), so neither leak was reproduced live.
  3. **`npm run audit` was Japanese-only *and* could not fail.** It hardcoded `src/data/ja`, so it was a **no-op for every other language while printing "ISSUES: none"** — and `RUNBOOK` §5 sells it as one of five gates. It now walks every language directory, takes a filter (`npm run audit -- es`), reports per-language totals, and keeps id-uniqueness global. Two exit-code holes closed at the same time, both instances of the same reassuring-green failure: **findings now set a non-zero exit** (it previously printed duplicates and issues and still exited 0, so it could never actually fail the gate), and **a bad filter argument is a hard error** (`npm run audit -- spanish` used to be dropped by the 2-letter regex and silently audit *everything* while printing a confident language list). All four exit paths verified, including against an injected duplicate id. It immediately picked up **566 French items it had never once opened**.
- [!] **🔴 MERGE DAY — Spanish is RED combined: 33 validation errors, and the fix is a judgement call, not a dedupe.** Measured 2026-08-05 by dry-merging all three es blocks onto the fix branch. Each block is green alone; together `validate:content` fails with **33 duplicate-front errors** (66 in `lint:curriculum`) — precisely the failure mode the merge seat exists to catch. Breakdown: **block 3 re-teaches 23 of block 1's words**, **block 2 re-teaches 7**, **block 3 re-teaches 3 of block 2's**. In git only `BUILD-CHECKLIST.md` conflicted; the content directories never collided, exactly as the runbook predicts.
  **Do not resolve this mechanically.** "Lower slot number wins" would delete block 3's copies, but the collisions split into two kinds that deserve opposite answers:
  - **Block 2's 7** (`el museo`, `el coche`, `el cielo`, `el año`, `el ojo`, `el día`, `hoy`) are true duplicates. Block 1's sounds unit legitimately owns them; block 2 should use them in examples and drop its cards. Lower-slot-wins is right here.
  - **Block 3's 23 are mostly function words** — `es`, `hay`, `de`, `en`, `con`, `un`, `una`, `son`, `yo`, `tú`, `mi`, `mis`, `pero`, `también`, `menos`, `siempre`. Block 1 picked these up *incidentally*, to build a sounds unit out of real words; block 3's `u12 Grammar 1 — basic sentence` and `u13`/`u14` exist **specifically to teach them**. Applying lower-slot-wins here deletes the grammar units' actual subject matter and leaves the systematic treatment nowhere. The pedagogically right move is for **block 1 to cede the function words to block 3**, keeping only the content words its sound demos need.
  **This is the pilot's headline finding.** Word ownership by slot number optimises for the wrong thing when an early unit *uses* a function word that a later grammar unit is built to *teach*. `RUNBOOK` §4/§7 should say so — "lower slot wins **for content words**; a function word belongs to the unit that teaches it, not the one that first uses it" — before the next language repeats it at scale. Related process hole: block 1's hand-forward note listing its consumed anchors was written *after* blocks 2 and 3 had already authored, so it never reached them. That note has to live on the **scaffold branch before the crews start**, not on block 1's branch afterwards.
  **Why this is escalated rather than fixed:** because **merge day belongs to the merge seat** (`RUNBOOK` §6 step 2 assigns "fix in the merged tree" there, and §0 says merge seats run one at a time), and this needs Alex's ruling on ownership first. An earlier draft justified the deferral as "it spans two other seats' content" — **that was wrong and the truth-agent called it**: the resolution I actually recommend (block 1 cedes its function words) lives entirely in `src/data/es/unit1..6` on `content/es-a1-block1`, which is my own block, my own lane. Only block 2's seven duplicates sit in someone else's files. The honest ground is "I'm not the merge seat", not "they're not my files".

## Idea CC — feature pitches (logged by Idea CC — the ideation lane: proposes, builds nothing)

**Who/what:** Idea CC scans the learning-science + ND-UX space and the current app, and files **ranked, concrete, ready-to-build proposals** here for the Feature (or Curriculum) lane to pick up. Every pitch is mission-aligned (deep understanding over memorization, mechanics over dopamine, ND-first) and grounded in real file refs. Idea CC **builds nothing** — a pitch becomes work only when a lane picks it up and Alex greenlights it; big greenlit pitches get expanded into a `BUILD-BRIEF-*.md`. See CLAUDE.md → "Roles."

*Ranking key:* **[R#]** = impact-per-effort rank within the batch (R1 = do first). Lane tag on every item. Nothing here is committed until Alex says go.

### Batch 2 — sentence & grammar card tier (2026-07-05 brainstorm; Alex's sentence-builder + Idea CC)

**Why now:** the word-level roster is SATURATED (see roster update above). Every card tests a word or a word-in-a-sentence (cloze); **nothing tests the *sentence* itself or a *grammar transformation*.** That's the next tier — where the grammar units (U19–21: copula, particles, ～ます/ました, い/な-adj conjugation) finally get *active production* instead of recognition. Alex's "sentence builder" is the flagship.

**🔑 Shared keystone — a JA sentence tokenizer.** R11/R12 (and optionally R10) all need to split a space-less kana/kanji example sentence into **word + particle tokens**. Feasible via **greedy longest-match over the known-vocab fronts + the closed particle set** (examples are short, space-less, and built only from globally-unique already-taught fronts — the vocab-front uniqueness validator guarantees it). When a sentence won't tokenize cleanly, the card simply isn't offered (safe degradation, exactly like `canCloze`). **Build the tokenizer once → three cards ride it.** Recommend one combined brief: **tokenizer + sentence builder (R11)**, then R10/R12 fall out cheaply.

- [ ] **[R10] (Feature CC — cheapest, highest value-per-effort) Particle cloze — `cloze:particle`.** Blank the **particle** in `example.jp` (`＿` where を/が/に/で/へ/は/と/も/の/か sits), learner picks the right one from the closed particle set. The single most-drilled grammar pain point, and a genuinely distinct skill from the shipped word-cloze. **Rides the shipped cloze card** — reuses its render + `deriveGrade({kind:"mc"})`; options are the fixed particle set (no distractor-building needed). Guard: the sentence has exactly one clearly-identifiable target particle (via the tokenizer, or a tiny content tag on the target token). Smallest of the four.
- [ ] **[R11] (Feature CC — brief-worthy, FLAGSHIP — Alex's idea) Sentence builder — `build:sentence`.** Scramble the **word + particle tokens** of `example.jp` into tiles; learner reassembles them in the correct order. Add 1–2 **distractor particle tiles** so it tests particle *choice*, not just ordering. It's the token-granularity version of the shipped `build` card (which assembles a *reading* from syllable tiles) — reuse that tile mechanic + `deriveGrade({kind:"typed"})`. Tests **word order + particle placement** = the core of production grammar. Needs the tokenizer keystone; guard `canBuildSentence`. Slots at the PRODUCED tier (rung 3). **This is the one to brief first.**
- [ ] **[R12] (Feature CC — rides R11) English → Japanese sentence production — `produce:sentence`.** Show only `example.en`, JA hidden; learner builds the JA sentence from tiles (R11's mechanic + a pool of plausible distractor words/particles). Because the reference sentence is hidden, it's **genuine production from meaning** — the deepest production short of free writing, yet ND-safe (tile assembly, not a blank page). Reuses R11's tokenizer + tile UI. Slots at top-of-PRODUCED / pre-SPOKEN — the "can you say it in Japanese?" bar, in tile form.
- [ ] **[R13] (Feature CC — ⚠️ needs new content data) Conjugation transform — `conjugate`.** Given a base/dictionary form + a target inflection (past ました · neg ません · plain ない · い-adj くない · past-adj かった · want たい), learner produces the conjugated form (tiles or typed → reuse `checkReading`). **Nothing tests grammatical *transformation* today**, and A1's whole grammar tail *is* conjugation. The one card with a real content cost: it needs **conjugation-pair data** (base → {past, neg, …}) = a schema/content addition (Curriculum + `contract.js`), unlike R10–R12 which reuse existing `example` data. Highest grammar-transformation value; ranked last only for that data dependency. *Route the data half to Curriculum CC once scoped.*

## QA findings (logged by QA CC — a third CC lane: tests + reports, does not build/author)

**Who/what:** QA CC runs the full local gate (`validate:content` → `lint:curriculum` → `test:unit` → `audit` → `build`) plus real-app/manual checks, and files prioritized findings here. QA does **not** author content or build features — it fixes only outright bugs / small-unambiguous defects and routes everything else to the Feature or Curriculum lane. See CLAUDE.md → "Three CC lanes."

**Baseline (2026-06-30, updated):** validate 0 err / 0 warn · lint 0 err / **1 advisory** (`ja-u16l6` 3 word cards, recommend 5–8 — yōon-tail, expected) · audit clean (**21 units / 93 lessons / 729 items / 0 dup ids**) · **55/55 unit tests** · build green. Tree is healthy. *(Note: this session the tree grew 20→21 units mid-run — `unit21.js` ぶんぽう・3 synced in via OneDrive while I worked. See P2 below.)*

### CLOSED — reset/sync verified by Alex on a real device (2026-09-05)

**Alex: "Reset works."** The one item in the 100-commit release that no automated environment could reach is confirmed working against live Supabase. Closed.

- **Verified:** sign in -> reset -> the account-attached path. Alex ran it on a real signed-in device, which is the only place `AUTH_ENABLED` is true.
- **Not separately confirmed:** the double-reset RACE (reset again without waiting for the toast, force-close inside a second). Recorded as unknown rather than assumed — if Alex only exercised the settled path, the race is still untested. Not a blocker; the receipt is the thing that was at risk and it works.
- The stop condition never fired: no report of "saved on this device" while signed in, which would have meant the account was not attached.

**Original entry, kept for the record:**

### DEFERRED BY ALEX — reset/sync verification (2026-09-02)

**Shipped to prod unverified, knowingly.** `main` `9a3311b5` was pushed with the reset/sync fix never exercised against a live Supabase. Alex was told the risk twice and chose to ship and revisit — recorded so the decision is traceable and the item is not lost.

- **What is unverified:** sign in -> load progress -> Settings -> Reset everything -> wait for "Progress reset — saved to your account" -> force-close -> reopen (must still be reset). Then the RACE: repeat WITHOUT waiting for the toast, force-close within a second, reopen.
- **Stop condition:** if the toast ever reads "saved on this device" while signed in, the account is not attached — a different and worse bug.
- **Why no automated test can cover it:** `App.jsx:32` sets `AUTH_ENABLED = supabase configured && !IS_WEBDRIVER`. Under Playwright it is false, so auth and onboarding never render; spoofing `navigator.webdriver` flips it true and the run lands on the login wall instead. **The same flag gates audio playback**, so no single automated run can have both app access and audio. Only a real signed-in device closes this.
- **Blast radius if wrong:** real user progress — the one item among the 100 merged commits that touches persisted learner state.

### QA pass before the four-branch merge + three new languages (2026-08-30)

**Verdict: the merge is safe to run; the two real blockers are NOT merge problems.** Scratch branch `qa/merge-verify` (kept; worktree removed) carries the whole stack — 4 branches, then the 3 scaffolds — so every resolution below is inspectable.

**JOB 1 — the merge works. ZERO conflicts across all four, including both files expected to collide.**
